specimen_label: Cadaveric prosection of lower leg and foot
transcribed_question: A) IDENTIFY THE TIED STRUCTURE B B) INJURY TO THE TIED STRUCTURE C IS CALLED?

marker.description: Blue thread tied around a tendon on the anterior aspect of the ankle.

main_question: Identify the structure indicated by the blue thread.
main_explanation: The blue thread indicates a tendon on the anterior aspect of the ankle, lateral to the tibia, which is part of the anterior compartment of the leg. This tendon typically divides into four slips to insert into the lateral four toes, characteristic of the extensor digitorum longus tendon.

supporting_question.question: Which nerve innervates the muscle associated with this tendon?
supporting_question.explanation: The extensor digitorum longus muscle, located in the anterior compartment of the leg, is innervated by the deep fibular nerve (a branch of the common fibular nerve).

true_false.statement: The extensor digitorum longus muscle originates from the lateral condyle of the tibia and the anterior surface of the fibula.
true_false.explanation: The extensor digitorum longus originates from the lateral condyle of the tibia, the upper three-quarters of the anterior surface of the fibula, and the interosseous membrane.
